summary: 作者从人类愿意照料其他物种的现象追溯人与动物的关系，并提出狩猎、分享有关动物的信息和长期接触，可能分别推动了工具使用、语言发展与驯化。
logic: 由饲养动物的现象发问
追溯工具与狩猎的转变

paragraphs.brief: 与动物密切相处是人类共同特征
sentences: Travel anywhere and you see something so common it may not even catch your attention.
旅行到任何地方，你就会看到一些很常见的东西可能不会引起你的注意
Wherever there are people, animals are being walked, herded and fed.
凡是有人生活的地方，都能看到人们遛动物、放牧或喂养动物。
Many, such as dogs, cats and sheep, are domesticated, but you will also find people living alongside wild creatures like monkeys and wolves.
其中许多是狗、猫、羊等驯化动物，但也有人与猴、狼等野生动物为邻。
Close contact with animals is not confined to one particular culture, region or ethnic group but is a universal human trait.
与动物的密切接触并不限于某一文化、区域或族裔群体，而是人类的普遍特征。
paragraphs.gist: 从遛狗、牧羊到与野生猴狼为邻，和其他动物密切相处的现象跨越地域与文化，是人类生活中极为普遍的特征。

paragraphs.brief: 跨物种照料的演化悖论
sentences: On the face of it this makes little sense.
从表面上看，这说不通
No other mammal adopts individuals from another species, with good reason.
没有其他哺乳动物收养来自其他物种的个体，有充分的理由。
Since the ultimate prize in evolution is perpetuating your genes, providing food for another species is counterproductive to success.
从演化角度看，首要的是让自己的基因延续下去，为其他物种提供食物反而不利于此。
Even if pets offer friendship, that cannot explain why our bond with other species arose in the first place.
即使宠物提供友谊也不能解释为什么我们与其他物种的关系一开始就存在
Who would bring a ferocious wolf into their home in the hope that thousands of years later it would become a loving pet?
谁会把凶猛的狼带进他们的家期望几千年后它会变成爱宠物呢？
paragraphs.gist: 从传递自身基因的角度看，耗用食物照料别的物种似乎得不偿失，而今日宠物带来的陪伴也解释不了祖先当初为何亲近野狼。

paragraphs.brief: 工具、语言和驯化共享的线索
sentences: As an anthropologist I have tried to understand this puzzle by looking to the past for the origins of our link with animals.
身为人类学家，我尝试回到过去，寻找人与动物联系的起源，以解开这个谜。
What I found was a long and unbroken evolutionary trail of evidence I call the ‘animal connection’.
我发现了一条漫长而连续的演化证据链，我称它为「人与动物的联结」。
This trail links to three important developments in human evolution: tool making, language and domestication.
这条线索串起人类演化中的三项重要发展：工具制造、语言和驯化。
If I am correct, and I believe that further research will conclusively show that I am, the animal connection is a hugely significant force instrumental in our global success.
如果我的看法正确——我相信进一步研究会给予确证——这种联结就是人类走向全球、取得成功的一股重要力量。
paragraphs.gist: 作者沿演化证据追溯人与动物的长期联系，主张这种联系贯穿工具制造、语言和驯化三个转折，并帮助人类在全球生存下来。

paragraphs.brief: 石器使祖先走上捕食者道路
sentences: The trail begins at least 2.6 million years ago.
至少260万年前这条路就开始了
That is when the first tools appear in the archaeological record.
这是考古记录中第一种工具出现的时候。
This development required the intellectual breakthrough of realizing that the properties of an object can be altered.
这种发展需要知识突破，即认识到物体的特性可以改变。
Man learnt how to turn stone into small, sharp items that could cut up animal carcasses, providing them with an evolutionary shortcut to becoming predators.
人类学会把石头制成小而锋利的工具，用来分割动物尸体，这使他们在成为捕食者的演化道路上走了捷径。
paragraphs.gist: 至少二百六十万年前出现的石器表明，人类已能有意识地改变物体性质，把石头制成利刃来分割动物尸体，从而更快成为捕食者。

paragraphs.brief: 狩猎改变饮食、竞争与迁徙
sentences: There were many consequences of the new hunting lifestyle.
新的狩猎生活方式有许多后果。
On the plus side, eating more meat and fat was a requirement for the increase in relative brain size.
一方面，食用更多的肉和脂肪是增加相对大脑规模的一个要求。
And since meat tends to come in bigger packages than leaves and roots, meat eaters could spend less time finding food and more on activities like learning and social interaction.
肉类一次能提供的食物通常比叶子和根多，因此食肉者耗在觅食上的时间减少，可以花更多时间学习和社交。
On the minus side, preying on animals put our ancestors into direct competition with the other predators that shared their ecosystem, animals such as lions and hyenas.
在负面上猎食动物令我们的祖先与分享其生态系统的其他掠食者诸如狮子和土狼等动物直接竞争
To get the upper hand, they needed more than just tools, and that is where the animal connection comes in.
要占据优势，他们所需的不只是工具，人与动物的联结正是在这里发挥了作用。
What made it possible for our ancestors to compete successfully with true carnivores was the ability to pay very close attention to the habits of both potential prey and competitors.
使我们的祖先能够成功地与真正的食肉动物竞争的是能够非常密切地关注潜在猎物和竞争者的习惯。
Knowledge was power, so we acquired a deep understanding of the minds of other animals.
知识是力量，所以我们深入了解了其他动物的思想。
Another significant consequence of becoming more predatory was the need to live at lower densities, as successful predators soon exhaust food supplies.
以捕猎为生还带来另一个重要后果：人群必须分散居住，因为善于捕猎的人很快就会耗尽一地的食物。
The record of the geographic distribution of our ancestors provides further support for my idea that the animal connection has shaped our evolution.
我们祖先的地理分布记录进一步证实了我的看法，即动物联系决定了我们的进化。
Early man lived in Africa and nowhere else, but then underwent a dramatic expansion in territory, forced by the search for new hunting grounds.
早期人生活在非洲，没有其他地方，但随后由于寻找新的狩猎场，领土急剧扩张。
paragraphs.gist: 食肉供给能量并省下觅食时间，却使人类与狮子等竞争；熟悉猎物和对手的习性帮助人类胜出，寻找新猎场又推动了地域扩张。

paragraphs.brief: 史前艺术以动物为中心
sentences: Throughout the period of these enormous changes in the lifestyle of our ancestors, gathering, sharing and recording knowledge became increasingly advantageous, and examples of prehistoric art that appear in Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia allow us to eavesdrop on their conversations.
在整个我们祖先生活方式的这些巨大变化期间，知识的收集、分享和记录越来越有利，欧洲、亚洲、非洲和澳大利亚出现的史前艺术实例使我们能够窃听他们的谈话。
Through the art, we realize the main topic was animals: their colours, shapes, postures and habits.
这些艺术让我们看出，他们最常交流的是动物的颜色、形状、姿势和习性。
This focus is even more striking considering that scenes of human life are rarely depicted.
考虑到人们很少描述人的生命场景，这一重点就更加引人注目。
Pictures of people, social interaction and ceremonies are rare.
人物、社交活动与仪式的图像都很少见。
paragraphs.gist: 多个大洲的史前艺术反复描摹动物的体色、姿态和习性，却很少表现人的社交活动，透露出祖先最重视交流和记录的知识。

paragraphs.brief: 交流动物知识与语言起源
sentences: This leads me on to the development of language.
这就引出了语言的发展问题。
Nobody doubts this proved a major adaptive advantage to our ancestors in developing complex behaviours.
没有人怀疑，这证明是我们祖先在发展复杂行为方面的主要适应优势。
How it arose, however, remains a mystery.
然而，它是如何产生的，仍然是个谜。
I believe I am the first to propose a continuity between the strong human-animal link that appeared 2.6 million years ago and the origin of language.
我认为，我是首位将二百六十万年前就存在的人与动物之间的密切关系，同语言起源视为连续发展过程的人。
The complexity and importance of animal-related information, indicated in the predominance of animal images, spurred early humans to move beyond what other species could achieve.
与动物有关的信息的复杂性和重要性，体现在动物图像占优势上，促使早期人类超越其他物种所能达到的目标。
Vervet monkeys, for example, have different cries for eagles and snakes, but they cannot discuss what threats might appear tomorrow.
例如，黑长尾猴遇到鹰与蛇会发出不同的叫声，却无法讨论明天可能发生的威胁。
The property of full language is that it is comprised of vocabulary and grammatical rules that can be combined in an infinite number of ways to convey fine shades of meaning.
完整语言的特点是有词汇和语法规则，可以无穷组合，传达意义的细微差别。
paragraphs.gist: 作者推测，复杂而重要的动物信息推动了语言发展：区别于猴子针对眼前危险的叫声，词汇和语法能组合出无数细微含义。

paragraphs.brief: 最早驯化的狼挑战食物储备说
sentences: As our ancestors became more involved with animals, the third product of the animal connection appeared: domestication, which has long been linked with the keeping of animals like sheep.
随着我们的祖先越来越多地与动物接触，动物连接的第三个产物出现了：驯化，它长期以来一直与饲养象羊一样的动物联系在一起。
Domestic animals are usually considered as ‘walking larders’, or easy food sources, reflecting the idea that the basis of this change was a drive for greater food security.
家养动物常被看作「会走路的食品储藏室」，也就是易得的食物来源；这种说法反映了人们认为驯化源于保障食物供应的愿望。
Looking at the origins of domestication for clues to its underlying reasons, I found fundamental flaws in this idea.
我追溯驯化的起源、寻找根本原因时，发现这种解释有根本缺陷。
Instead, my analysis suggests domestication emerged as a natural progression of our close association with, and understanding of, other species.
我的分析表明，驯化是人类长期亲近和了解其他物种后自然发生的下一步。

If domestication was about knowing where your next meal was coming from, the first domesticate ought to have been a food source, yet analysis of fossils shows that the domestication of dogs pre-dated that of any other species, even plants, from wolves.
如果驯化是为了有饭可吃，最早被驯化的应是食用物种，但化石分析显示，狼被驯化为狗的时间，比任何其他动物甚至植物的驯化都早。
Furthermore, if the objective was to have meat to eat, you wouldn’t select an animal that eats two kilograms of meat a day.
而且，如果目标是有肉吃，你不会选择一个动物每天吃两公斤肉。
It was familiarity with this species that led to eventual domestication.
正是由于熟悉这种物种，才最终被驯化。
paragraphs.gist: 最早被驯化的竟是本身消耗大量肉食的狼而非食用动物，这使作者认为，驯化源于长期熟悉其他物种，而不能仅用储备食物解释。

items.en: Travellers are more likely to notice wild animals than domesticated ones.
items.zh: 旅行者更容易注意到野生动物，而较少留意家养动物。
items.why: 作者说人们旅行时可能忽略随处可见的人与动物共处现象，却没有比较旅行者更容易留意野生动物还是驯养动物。

items.en: All cultures demonstrate a need to have close contact with animals.
items.zh: 在所有文化中，人都有与动物密切接触的需要。
items.why: 作者明确说，与动物亲近不限于某个文化、地区或族群，而是人类共有的特征，覆盖了题干所说的所有文化。

items.en: Animals benefit from allowing other animal species to share food resources.
items.zh: 动物让其他物种分享自己的食物资源，对自身也有好处。
items.why: 从延续自身基因的角度看，把食物资源供给其他物种会妨碍自身利益。题干却说这种分享会让提供资源的动物获益。

items.en: It is unlikely that people initially domesticated wolves for future companionship.
items.zh: 人类最初驯化狼，很可能并不是为了日后与它们作伴。
items.why: 这是反问=作者态度: 几乎不可能有人当初为了“未来陪伴”去做这件事。题干的“unlikely”与反问语气一致” YES。

items.en: There are periods of human evolution for which we have little information about man’s relationship with animals.
items.zh: 对于人类演化中的某些时期，我们几乎不了解当时人与动物的关系。
items.why: 作者形容所发现的演化证据是一条漫长而连续、从未中断的轨迹，与题干所说某些时期缺乏相关信息相反。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: Around 2.6 million years ago, humans became predators after they realized the possibility of object ________.
items.zh: 大约260万年前，人类意识到可以对现有物品进行 ________，从此成为捕食者。
items.why: “altered/changed” = adaptation (改变以适应/改造)。其他词如 behavior/connection/ leadership 不表达“把物体改造成工具”的关键点。

items.en: Once humans were hunters, they benefited from better ________ and extra time which could be spent on non-physical activities.
items.zh: 人类开始狩猎以后，获得了更好的 ________，也多出了可以用于非体力活动的时间。
items.why: 回到对应内容“肉类一次能提供的食物通常比叶子和根多，因此食肉者耗在觅食上的时间减少，可以花更多时间学习和社交”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: However, the more humans came to depend on meat as a food source, the more ________ there was between them and other predators.
items.zh: 不过，人类越依赖肉类为食，与其他捕食者之间的 ________ 就越激烈。
items.why: 回到对应内容“在负面上猎食动物令我们的祖先与分享其生态系统的其他掠食者诸如狮子和土狼等动物直接竞争”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: It wasn’t a spear or knife that gave them this advantage, but the ________ skills that humans began to develop.
items.zh: 给人类带来这种优势的是他们开始发展的 ________ 技能，矛或刀本身并非关键。
items.why: “pay very close attention” = observation (观察)。不是 leadership (领导力),也不是 connection (联系),核心是“观察习性/读懂动物”。

items.en: Then, because humans were such successful predators, they required more ________ and this led to groups of people moving away from Africa.
items.zh: 人类狩猎卓有成效，于是需要更多 ________，这促使一些人群离开非洲。
items.why: 回到对应内容“早期人生活在非洲，没有其他地方，但随后由于寻找新的狩猎场，领土急剧扩张”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

items.en: What is the writer’s main argument in the sixth paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第六段的主要论点是什么？
correct: Early man valued the communication of knowledge about animal behaviour and appearance.
早期人类重视交流有关动物行为和外形的知识。

items.en: What is the writer doing in the seventh paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第七段采用了什么论述方式？
correct: making a claim about the way that language developed.
对语言的发展方式提出主张。

items.en: The writer refers to vervet monkeys in order to:
items.zh: 作者为什么提到黑长尾猴？
correct: highlight the sophistication of human communication.
突显人类交流的复杂程度。

items.en: The writer says that the ‘walking larder’ idea
items.zh: 对于把驯养动物看作“会走动的食物储藏室”这一说法，作者认为……
correct: fails to explain the purpose of domestication.
它无法解释人类驯化动物的目的。

pairs: 第 5 段 · 第 5 句
points: 作者说人们旅行时可能忽略随处可见的人与动物共处现象，却没有比较旅行者更容易留意野生动物还是驯养动物。
“altered/changed” = adaptation (改变以适应/改造)。其他词如 behavior/connection/ leadership 不表达“把物体改造成工具”的关键点。
clauses: If I am correct, and I believe …, the animal connection is a hugely significant force instrumental in our global success.
“that further research will conclusively show that I am”补足 believe 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 believe 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
As our ancestors became more involved with animals, the third product of the animal connection appeared: domestication, ….
“which has long been linked with the keeping of animals like sheep”修饰前面的 domestication。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 domestication，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Professor of anthropology Pat Shipman looks at the ways in which our relationships with animals have shaped our own human evolution.
人类学教授帕特·希普曼探讨人与动物的关系如何塑造人类自身的演化。
